findings.title: All-clients fallback NPEs when the Clients resource is missing
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) treats a missing per-client resource as an all-clients check, then calls PolicyStore.findByResource with whatever getResourceTypeResource returns. That helper returns null when the admin-permissions client has no "Clients" resource (schema not initialized, or an already-enabled realm that never received the new type). findByResource(server, null) then throws, so a normal manage/view/configure check becomes a 500 instead of a deny. The same null is later passed into ResourcePermission if the empty-policy guard is skipped.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the type resource name, not client ids
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission searches resources of type "Clients" and adds resource.getName() for every granted scope. The all-clients resource created by the schema is itself typed "Clients" and named "Clients", so a realm-wide grant inserts the literal "Clients" into the result and does not expand to actual client ids. Callers that filter client lists or role-mapping targets by this set will either hide every real client or treat a non-client id as granted. Per-client resources are only present after a specific permission was created, so an all-clients MAP_ROLES/VIEW grant cannot be applied through this API.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never get the Clients type or scopes
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and nothing else in this change creates the new Clients resource or the configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Realms that already enabled fine-grained admin permissions V2 therefore keep a schema that only has Users. Creating a Clients permission then fails scope validation ("No scopes found" / "Scope was not found for resource type"), and evaluation cannot fall back to an all-clients resource that was never stored.

findings.title: Client permission resources are not resolved to a display name
findings.body: getResourceName now has a Clients resource type whose stored name is the client UUID, but the method only special-cases Users and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Client resources are created with name set to the internal id and no display name, so admin permission listings show null (or a raw id) instead of the clientId. Deleting or renaming the client also has no equivalent of the user-not-found check, so stale client resources stay unlabeled.

findings.title: V2 client permission hooks throw instead of denying
findings.body: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now always returns ClientPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, but isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, canExchangeTo, resource, getPermissions, and the Policy accessors throw UnsupportedOperationException. Those methods are on the live admin evaluator path (client removal, permissions UI, token exchange). A caller that previously got false/null from the V1 evaluator now fails the request with 500, including for admins who only have realm roles and never opted into per-client policies.

findings.title: Client removal no longer cleans permissions when only V2 is enabled
findings.body: The removal listener is now skipped unless ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled. With only V2 enabled, ClientRemovedEvent does not run, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws anyway, so there is no cleanup of the authz resource named with the deleted client's id. A later permission evaluation can still grant scopes on that orphan id, and resource listings keep growing after clients are deleted.

findings.title: requireView javadoc describes a boolean return
findings.body: The new comments on requireView and requireViewClientScopes say they return true when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is true. Both methods are void and are documented elsewhere as throwing ForbiddenException. Implementors and callers reading only these comments will treat a failed check as a boolean instead of an authorization failure.
